supported.quote: With monthly-spend-feature on, account page requests reach `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. It integer-divides the month's spend total by the number of purchases marked as this month, and nothing guards against that list being empty.

A shopper who has bought before but not this month therefore raises ZeroDivisionError, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turns that error into a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

An admin switched on a new monthly spending summary for shoppers' account pages, and its calculation then failed with a division by zero, most likely for shoppers who had bought before but nothing yet this month, so their account pages failed to load.
Switching the monthly-spend-feature flag back on would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the logs report a rising account-page error rate.

The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code (src/io_shop/spend_summary.py). This error first appears in the minute the onset is dated to and was not seen before it.

The spend summary code ran on account page requests because admin switched the monthly-spend-feature flag on at {P1.1}. The logs show the flag evaluated off in every minute before that, split between off and on during that minute, and on in every minute after.
Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed {T15.2} flag change by anyone but Argus in the {T15.3} hour read, the switch of monthly-spend-feature.
The ClientDisconnected account-page failures: they occurred throughout the minutes before the onset, while the flag was still off.
With the flag on, the monthly spend summary divided by the number of the shopper's purchases this month, which is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.

No check was seen that would have limited the monthly-spend-feature flag to a small share of shoppers when it was first switched on, or watched errors as it went out. The flag was evaluated on for all traffic soon after the switch.

No test was seen that ran the monthly spend summary for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production. Code-Fix's reading says its new tests for that case would fail against the current code.

Code-Fix's reading of src/io_shop/account_page.py says the page's error boundary turned each error from the spend summary into a failed page. Nothing was seen that would render the page without the summary when the summary fails.
